metaTitle: Roofing SEO Services for Roofing Contractors
metaDescription: Roofing SEO from ASP: service pages, Google Business Profile, storm content and technical fixes, measured against booked jobs. No bought links.
intro: Roofing SEO is the work of getting your company found when homeowners search for roof repair, replacement or storm damage help, in the map pack and the organic results. ASP builds the service pages, Business Profile work and technical fixes behind that, and reports it against booked jobs.

sections.heading: What roofing SEO covers
paragraphs: Roofing SEO covers four pieces of work. The first is the service pages a homeowner reads before calling. The second is content that answers the questions they search. The third is the technical health that lets Google index all of it, and the fourth is the local signals behind map-pack placement. The same work feeds the AI answers that now sit above some search results.

For a roofer, the pages follow the work itself. BLS lists replacement, repair and new installation as what will drive demand for roofers, and notes that some may come from rooftop solar installs. A service with real search demand gets its own page, while one nobody searches for by name gets folded into a broader page.

sections.heading: Service pages and content built from your roofing jobs
paragraphs: Content that ranks says what the rest of the internet can't. We interview you or a senior member of your crew and pull out details only a roofer knows: what a tear-off cost last month, why a patch fails on an aging roof, and what you tell a homeowner before they ask.

We build content clusters in order of what a booked job is worth to you, not by search volume. A replacement page, for example, gets surrounded by the material comparison, the cost breakdown and the signs a roof needs replacing, all linked together.

Seasonal content follows the schedule homeowners are told to keep. In guidance published in 2013, the National Roofing Contractors Association recommended inspecting roofs at least twice a year, preferably in spring and fall. Inspection pages and posts timed to those seasons give a homeowner a reason to call before a leak forces it.

sections.heading: Google Business Profile and the map pack for roofers
paragraphs: Map-pack placement leans on your Business Profile, review volume and recency, and consistent citations. Google's guidelines say a business that serves customers at their location should keep one profile for its central office with a designated service area. A virtual office cannot be listed unless it is staffed during business hours, so an unstaffed address in each nearby town breaks the rules.

Local SEO Pro handles this side: profile management, citation audits across 60+ directories on a 90-day cycle, a monthly ranking heatmap from 50+ grid points, and local schema. Its report sits next to the organic work so the two are not pulling against each other.
For towns you serve without an office, service-area pages on your website carry the work.

sections.heading: Storm and weather content for roofing sites
paragraphs: Weather sets much of the roofing calendar. NOAA says hail can damage homes, and the corner where Nebraska, Colorado and Wyoming meet averages seven to nine hail days a year. BLS adds that roofers usually do not work in bad weather and that winter can limit work in northern states.

Two kinds of content handle that. Evergreen pages on hail damage, wind damage and storm inspections should be live and indexed well before storm season, so they are ready when searches spike. StormFront adds event posts: when a qualifying weather event hits your service area, it publishes location-aware content to your blog, Business Profile and social profiles.

sections.heading: Technical SEO for roofing websites
paragraphs: Google has to read a page before it can rank it. We check status codes, redirect chains, canonicals, schema, the sitemap and how fast pages load on a phone. Then we fix problems in order of what each one costs you, so an indexing issue blocking a dozen service pages comes before a slow hero image.
If your site carries large project galleries or before-and-after photos, those are worth keeping, and they need to be sized so they do not slow the page down on a phone.

sections.heading: How much roofing SEO costs
paragraphs: Market size includes the competition. BLS counted 26,626 private residential roofing contractor establishments nationally in 2025, but the number that matters for your price is how many of them compete in your zip codes and how strong their sites already are.
Organic SEO isn't sold here as a separate rate-card retainer. The audit sets the scope, and you see the number before you commit to anything.

ASP's published price points are Local SEO Pro at $1,200 a month, StormFront at $549 a month, Foundation at $2,500 a month and Growth at $3,850 a month, with Premier priced custom. The full breakdown is on our pricing page.
bullets: Market size: how many roofers compete for the same searches where you work.
Service area: a single town needs less work than a metro and its suburbs.
Services and locations: each service and each location with real demand needs its own page.
Technical debt: redirects, indexing problems and slow pages that have to be cleared first.

faqs.question: How long does roofing SEO take to show results?
faqs.answer: There is no honest fixed timeline. It depends on your site's history, the technical debt in the way and how competitive your market is. Technical fixes show first, on-page work moves next, and new content clusters are slowest but last longest.

faqs.question: Do you build backlinks for roofing websites?
faqs.answer: No. ASP does not buy links or sell link packages. Links that come from useful content, real partnerships and PR are worth having, and we let them come from the work.

faqs.question: Can I add a Google Business Profile for each town I serve?
faqs.answer: Not without an office there that is staffed during business hours. Google's guidelines say a service-area business should keep one profile for its central office with a service area set. Service-area pages on your website cover the other towns.

faqs.question: What is the difference between roofing SEO and Local SEO Pro?
faqs.answer: Local SEO Pro covers your Business Profile, citations, the ranking heatmap and local schema. Roofing SEO on this page covers keyword strategy, service pages, content depth and technical fixes. Most clients need both, and they report together.

faqs.question: How do you measure roofing SEO?
faqs.answer: Against booked revenue. Rankings and impressions show whether visibility is moving, leads show whether it is landing, and booked jobs show whether it paid. Where your CRM supports attribution, we carry lead source through to the job. Domain Authority is a third-party score Google does not use, so it is not in the report.

faqs.question: Will SEO help me get storm work after a hailstorm?
faqs.answer: It helps most when the pages are already in place. Hail and storm damage pages that are indexed before the season are ready when homeowners start searching. StormFront adds posts timed to qualifying weather events in your service area.

faqs.question: Do AI Overviews change roofing SEO?
faqs.answer: The work that earns a spot in AI answers is the same work that earns rankings: first-hand detail, clear authorship and a site that crawls cleanly. There is no separate file or markup that makes an AI cite you. What changes is measurement, because some searches end without a click.
